question: Why is it important to be transparent and honest when a community health project falls short of its goals?

options.C: It prevents the community from ever asking for help again
options.D: It maintains community trust and helps everyone learn what to improve

question: What protective action prevents food from entering the respiratory airway during a normal swallow?

question: If a brain tumor starts growing inside the skull, what has to happen first to keep pressure from rising too high?

question: When does a conflict of interest typically occur in a healthcare setting?

options.A: When an individual worker's goals clash directly with the demands of the health facility

options.C: When the hospital has an excess of funds and medical supplies
options.D: When patient satisfaction scores reach one hundred percent

explanation: Conflict happens when what you want to do (like resting or traveling) clashes with what the hospital urgently needs you to do (like covering a busy shift).

question: A bedridden patient on fluid restriction needs a daily weight check. What is the most important step to make sure the reading is correct?

options.A: Remove all intravenous lines temporarily during the weighing process
options.B: Use a standard bathroom floor scale slid underneath the mattress
options.C: Weigh the patient only when visitors are present to help
options.D: Ensure the bedding and drainage tubes are arranged consistently or zeroed out

question: Which part of the syringe driver securely holds the syringe plunger and pushes it forward?

options.A: The clear plastic needle cap
options.B: The external wall power plug

options.D: The digital display screen

question: What happens in the body when Beta-2 adrenergic receptors are stimulated?

options.A: Relaxation of smooth muscle in the airways
options.B: Decrease in overall heart rate and force
options.C: Constriction of peripheral blood vessels
options.D: Increased production of digestive fluids

question: At what centimeter of cervical dilation does the alert line on the partograph traditionally start?

question: What is the very first action a nurse must take when managing an active adverse drug reaction?

options.A: Discharging the patient home for proper rest
options.B: Calling the pharmaceutical manufacturing company
options.C: Starting broad-spectrum antibiotics immediately
options.D: Stopping the administration of the suspected drug

question: If a patient has a growth causing uncontrolled hypersecretion of a hormone, what happens?

options.A: Complete shutdown of all nervous system reflex pathways
options.B: An exaggerated physiological response and metabolic disturbance
options.C: Permanent cessation of all tropic hormone production
options.D: Immediate reversal of normal circadian rhythm patterns

question: How would you best describe depression in a clinical setting?

options.A: A temporary lack of vitamins causing physical weakness
options.B: A minor behavioral adjustment issue in older adults
options.C: A serious mood disorder affecting thoughts and daily activities
options.D: A temporary emotional reaction to physical fatigue

explanation: Spot on! Depression isn't just a brief bad mood or fatigue; it's a true mood disorder that impacts a person's entire daily life and well-being.

question: As a nurse, what is an important rule to remember when checking in on a traumatized patient?

options.A: Rely solely on written questionnaires handed out at the triage desk
options.B: Ignore non-verbal cues and focus entirely on laboratory values
options.C: Insist that the patient describe every frightening moment in detail
options.D: Avoid forcing the patient to recount traumatic details immediately

explanation: Spot on! Never pressure a survivor to retell a scary story before they are ready. Pushing too hard can actually re-traumatize them. Let them take their time. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h4)

question: Why is a 'just culture'—where nurses can report mistakes without fear of punishment—so important?

options.A: It removes all legal liability from the hospital organization
options.B: It encourages honest reporting of mistakes so systemic flaws can be fixed
options.C: It ensures that negligent staff members never face disciplinary action
options.D: It eliminates the need for incident report documentation

explanation: A just culture focuses on fixing broken systems rather than just blaming individuals. When people aren't terrified to speak up, everyone learns and patients stay safer!

question: Which of these choices is a MAJOR safety violation when handling hospital equipment?

options.A: Checking for frayed electrical cords
options.B: Obtaining informed consent from the patient
options.C: Skipping equipment cleaning to save time
options.D: Ensuring proper disinfection between patients

explanation: Never skip cleaning! Proper maintenance and disinfection protect patients from nasty infections and keep equipment running smoothly.

question: Why must public health measures continue even if a disease is wiped out in Nigeria?

options.A: Local health workers lose their medical licenses after an outbreak
options.B: The pathogen can still be imported from other regions where it exists
options.C: Patients will develop allergies if vaccination programs stop
options.D: Eliminated diseases always mutate into completely different organisms

explanation: As long as the germ is active in other parts of the world, travelers or animals can easily bring it back across borders. Stay alert!

question: What dangerous hazard is often associated with bulging food cans?

options.A: High vitamin C loss

options.C: Natural yeast fermentation
options.D: Botulinum toxins

question: What color is a healthy, normal tympanic membrane?

options.A: Dark yellow
options.B: Bright red

options.D: Pearly-gray

question: What is the minimum number of days between periods that defines oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: 35 days
options.B: 60 days
options.C: 45 days
options.D: 21 days

explanation: You've got this! Oligomenorrhoea simply means menstrual cycles that are unusually spread out, lasting longer than 35 days. Think of it as infrequent periods.

question: A pregnant patient complains of severe lower back ache after standing for hours at her market stall. What is the main cause?

options.A: Inflammation of the bone marrow inside the vertebrae

options.C: Direct pressure of the fetal head on the lumbar nerves

explanation: The muscles along the lower spine have to work overtime to keep the body upright against the forward pull of pregnancy, leading to tiredness and aches.

question: Why can assigning biological sex at birth based only on external genitals sometimes be tricky?

options.A: Hormone levels are impossible to measure in newborns
options.B: External genitalia change completely during the first year of life
options.C: Chromosomes are always identical in every human being
options.D: Internal organs and chromosomes can occasionally differ from external physical appearance

explanation: You've got this! Genitals are just one part of biological sex; variations in chromosomes or internal anatomy mean external looks don't always tell the whole story.

question: How does blocking sequential steps in a biochemical pathway create synergy?

options.A: It forces the liver to excrete both medications immediately
options.B: It tricks the immune system into ignoring the medications
options.C: It neutralizes all toxic byproducts before they reach organs
options.D: It cuts off multiple survival routes for a target cell or pathogen

explanation: Imagine blocking all exits in a room. By hitting a pathogen at two different steps, you trap it with nowhere left to run!

question: What key role do community health nurses play when working with incoming NGO teams?

options.A: Managing financial audits for donor agencies
options.B: Funding the operational budgets of international organizations
options.C: Acting as a liaison to coordinate outreach schedules with local clinics
options.D: Drafting national health legislation in the federal assembly

explanation: Nurses are the vital bridge between visiting NGOs and local primary health centers, keeping patient care organized and steady.

question: Which landmark document formally launched the modern health promotion movement in 1986?

options.A: The Alma-Ata Declaration
options.B: The Abuja Declaration
options.C: The Nightingale Pledge
options.D: The Ottawa Charter

explanation: The Ottawa Charter of 1986 defined the core strategies for health promotion on a global scale. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why does stopping your antibiotics halfway through cause drug resistance?

options.A: It forces the body to produce too many white blood cells
options.B: It makes the remaining tablets expire much faster in storage
options.C: It allows the strongest bacteria to survive, mutate, and multiply
options.D: It immediately cures the viral infection causing the fever

explanation: Exactly! Stopping early kills only the weak germs, leaving the tough, stubborn bacteria alive to multiply and become resistant to future drugs.

question: In a hospital pharmacy, what does the FEFO inventory rule stand for?

options.A: Free Essential Formulas Only
options.B: Financial Evaluation For Operations
options.C: First-Expired, First-Out
options.D: Fastest Earnings From Outpatients

explanation: Easy and practical! FEFO means you sell the drugs that expire sooner first, so valuable medicine doesn't go to waste on the shelf.

question: What happens if a vaccine meant for a muscle (intramuscular) is accidentally given into the fatty layer under the skin?

options.A: Severe systemic toxicity and high fever
options.B: Poor absorption leading to a weaker immune response
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the local muscle
options.D: Immediate destruction of the vaccine by skin enzymes

explanation: Fatty tissue doesn't have as rich a blood supply as muscle, so the vaccine doesn't get absorbed properly to do its job. Technique matters!

question: What does the term 'reduction' mean in the management of fractures?

options.A: Gradual shrinking of local soft tissue swelling using ice packs
options.B: Lowering the patient's blood pressure prior to orthopedic surgery
options.C: Surgical removal of dead bone tissue from an infected site
options.D: Realignment of the broken bone fragments into their normal position

explanation: Reduction is the process of putting displaced bone ends back into their correct anatomical alignment so they can heal properly. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h5)

question: What is a major problem caused by constant political leadership changes in public health?

options.A: Disruption of long-term strategic health plans
options.B: Automatic increase in staff salaries nationwide
options.C: Total elimination of bureaucratic red tape
options.D: Immediate improvement in hospital equipment supply

explanation: So true! When political bosses change too often, great health projects are often abandoned mid-way, slowing down progress.

question: What is the main goal of mobile medical outreaches for persons with disabilities in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: To gather statistical research data without providing direct care
options.B: To replace all permanent primary healthcare clinics in the country
options.C: To conduct advanced surgical operations in local village squares
options.D: To bring essential healthcare services and assistive devices closer to underserved populations

explanation: Outreach brings care right to the doorsteps of people who can't easily travel to big city hospitals. Vital work for community health!

question: Why are elderly patients often at a higher risk of becoming dehydrated?

options.A: Water moves faster through older digestive tracts
options.B: Their bodies require less water than teenagers
options.C: They store more water in their skin tissues
options.D: They often experience a reduced sense of thirst

explanation: Correct! As people age, their natural thirst cue slows down, meaning they might not feel thirsty even when their body desperately needs water.

question: What do we mean by the 'second victim' in healthcare?

options.A: The family members who witness a patient's decline
options.B: The secondary patient sharing a room with the affected individual
options.C: The healthcare professionals who experience emotional trauma after an error
options.D: The hospital institution that faces lawsuits and financial fines

explanation: The 'second victim' is the nurse or doctor who suffers deep emotional pain and stress after being involved in an unexpected patient incident.

question: Unlike fats and carbohydrates, why do we need to eat protein-rich foods every single day?

options.A: Muscles consume all available protein within four hours
options.B: The liver destroys all stored amino acids overnight
options.C: The body does not have a dedicated storage depot for protein
options.D: Proteins evaporate quickly through the skin pores

explanation: Our bodies store extra carbs as glycogen and extra fat in adipose tissue, but we don't have a storage warehouse for protein. That's why daily dietary intake is a must!

question: Which action is a serious legal violation in healthcare financial administration?

options.A: Reporting an unfavorable budget variance to the hospital director
options.B: Collaborating with finance officers to review monthly shift overtime
options.C: Documenting medical procedures that were never actually performed
options.D: Using generic brand dressings instead of expensive name brands

question: Which of the following interventions requires skilled nursing rather than basic custodial care?

options.A: Helping a client put on a shirt and button up the front

options.C: Cutting meat into small pieces on a plate during lunch
options.D: Changing a complex surgical wound dressing and monitoring an IV line

question: What happens when the sleep-promoting centers quiet down the reticular activating system?

options.A: Metabolic rate spikes rapidly

question: How do convulsions and seizures relate to each other?

options.A: All seizures are convulsions, but not all convulsions are seizures

options.C: All convulsions are seizures, but not all seizures are convulsions

question: Why is good record-keeping so important when multiple nurses are checking in on the same pregnant woman?

options.A: It replaces the need to talk directly with the mother

options.C: It prevents errors and ensures everyone knows the current care plan
options.D: It is only needed for statistical counting at the end of the year

question: What happens during opsonization?

options.A: Viruses are blocked from entering healthy cells by sticky chemical covers.

question: A CT scan image shows a cross-section of the abdomen dividing it into top and bottom halves. Which plane was used?

question: How does palliative care differ from curative care when dealing with advanced chronic illness?

options.A: Palliative care eliminates the need for any nursing or medical supervision

question: Why should a performance review session be a two-way conversation?

options.A: It speeds up the meeting so everyone can return to patient care faster
options.B: It legally prevents the nurse from ever receiving a low grade
options.C: It ensures the manager does not have to prepare any written notes

question: Which of these is an immediate complication you might see right after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage
options.B: Chronic pelvic pain

question: How do alpha-1 blockers help a patient with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)?

question: When planning meals for a pregnant patient in your community, what should guide you the most?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on raw vegetable diets
options.B: Using only expensive imported vitamin supplements
options.C: Eliminating all traditional family recipes

question: A chronic disease has very few new cases each year, yet a high number of people live with it for decades. What will the statistics show?

options.A: Low incidence and high prevalence

question: What is an important nursing task to do right after a patient finishes eating to lower their risk of pneumonia?

question: A nurse changes a contaminated needle but reuses the plastic syringe barrel for another patient. What is the big danger here?

question: Why is solar drying an effective traditional preservation method for grains and legumes?

question: How do NGOs commonly help out rural health posts?

options.D: Owning and operating commercial banks

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluating a health communication program?

options.C: Monitoring tracks daily activities, while evaluation measures long-term impact
options.D: Monitoring focuses on drugs, while evaluation focuses only on surgery

question: A healthy traveler arrives from a country experiencing a dangerous viral outbreak. What public health action is most appropriate for this traveler?

options.A: Immediate discharge

options.C: Isolation
options.D: Surgical debridement

question: What is the primary purpose of evaluating a community health program?

question: Why must a nurse remember that not every large or palpable mass in the genitourinary area is cancer?

question: A patient with advanced cancer starts strong opioid pain medication. What preventive care must you include?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to prevent fluid overload from the oral medications

options.C: Checking blood pressure every fifteen minutes to monitor for sudden hypertension

question: What is the main purpose of the evaluation step in the nursing process?

options.A: To write the initial medical diagnosis for the patient chart
options.B: To perform the physical head-to-toe baseline assessment
options.C: To administer emergency medications during a crisis
options.D: To determine if the patient met the established care goals

explanation: Exactly! Evaluation is where you check the patient's progress to see if your care plan actually worked or needs a tweak.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of inaccurate pulse oximeter readings?

options.A: Severe cold hands with poor circulation
options.B: Normal room temperature lighting
options.C: Patient movement and shivering
options.D: Dark nail polish on the finger

question: In basic terms, what is a poison?

options.A: Any substance that disrupts body functions or causes harm when introduced

options.C: A chemical compound that only harms the liver and kidneys
options.D: An infectious microorganism found in contaminated water sources

explanation: Spot on! A poison is simply anything that enters the body and causes harm or upsets normal body functions. You've got this!

question: What is the main role of the thymus gland in the human body?

options.A: Regulating blood sugar levels after meals

options.C: Maturing T-lymphocytes for the immune system
options.D: Filtering bacteria out of swallowed food

question: Why do problems in the brain-testicle hormone pathway (hypothalamic-pituitary-testicular axis) often affect both sperm and testosterone?

question: Why is the skin considered our body's primary shield?

options.A: It sits right between our internal organs and the outside world.

options.C: It pumps nutrients directly into underlying muscles.
options.D: It filters waste straight out of our bloodstream.

question: During the dry season, which water source is most risky for catching Guinea worm?

options.C: A rapid-flowing mountain stream with rocky beds
options.D: A deep concrete borehole with a hand pump

question: Why must a nurse be extra careful when cutting the nails of a patient with diabetes?

options.A: Clipping nails makes blood sugar shoot up instantly
options.B: Decreased sensation means minor injuries can go unnoticed and lead to severe ulcers
options.C: Special clippers for diabetics can shock them
options.D: Diabetic nails grow much faster than normal

question: What is the main job of the glomerulus when making urine?

options.A: Reabsorbing essential glucose back into the bloodstream

options.D: Storing urine until it is ready for elimination

question: What is the main goal of "value clarification" workshops for nursing staff?

options.A: To train nurses on advanced surgical procedures like abdominal hysterectomy
options.B: To enforce strict legal penalties against patients who induce abortions
options.C: To help nurses set aside personal biases to provide non-judgmental care

question: During a clinic health talk, you want to recommend affordable local Nigerian foods rich in iron. Which of these is best?

question: Why might a vaccine that works brilliantly in a research lab fail to protect a community completely in real life?

options.C: Laboratory tests use synthetic antigens that behave differently than real viruses

question: A 40-year-old client with a desk job and a high body weight asks about their risk for diabetes. What is the best nursing explanation?

options.A: Physical inactivity and excess weight increase cellular resistance to insulin

question: When should you release the pulled skin tissue when doing a Z-track injection?

options.C: After the needle has been completely withdrawn
options.D: While the needle is still inside the muscle tissue

explanation: Keep holding that skin until the needle is completely out! Letting go only after the needle is gone ensures the track zips shut and traps the medicine inside.

question: How do vaccines primarily protect the human body against infectious diseases?

options.A: By lowering body temperature during an active viral infection
options.B: By destroying bacteria directly with heavy doses of antibiotics
options.C: By stimulating the immune system to produce protective antibodies
options.D: By cleaning harmful toxins directly out of the bloodstream

explanation: Vaccines teach the immune system to recognize and fight off specific germs safely. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient took a drug that leaves the body mainly through urine. As a nurse, how can you help speed up this process?

options.A: Administering prescribed intravenous fluids to promote urine output
options.B: Inserting a nasogastric tube for continuous suction
options.C: Restricting all oral and IV fluids
options.D: Applying external cooling blankets

explanation: Hydration is key! Giving IV fluids helps the kidneys produce enough urine to safely flush water-soluble toxins out of the body.

question: An asthma patient taking steroid medications suddenly has high blood sugar readings. What should you suspect?

options.A: Severe dehydration from lack of water intake
options.B: Medication-induced alteration of glucose metabolism
options.C: A primary failure of the pancreas to produce insulin
options.D: An allergic reaction to the asthma medication

explanation: Spot on! Steroid therapy frequently messes with normal blood sugar control, even in people who have never had diabetes before.

question: What tiny helper in the small intestine makes oral rehydration solution (ORS) work so well?

options.A: Passive diffusion through stomach fat
options.B: Active protein pump rejection
options.C: Sodium-glucose cotransporters
options.D: Renal tubular reabsorption

explanation: Glucose teams up with sodium to pull water quickly across the gut wall, making ORS a brilliant tool against dehydration.

question: Why does metabolic acidosis happen during prolonged shock?

options.A: Cells switch to anaerobic metabolism and produce lactic acid
options.B: Carbon dioxide dissolves directly into the circulating blood plasma
options.C: The kidneys stop filtering hydrogen ions from the bloodstream
options.D: Excessive oxygen enters the cells and lowers blood pH

explanation: Great job thinking about cellular metabolism! When cells don't get enough oxygen, they switch to backup (anaerobic) energy production. This leaves behind lactic acid as waste, which lowers blood pH and causes acidosis.

question: What is a major downside of relying only on external rewards (like money or gifts) to motivate staff?

options.A: It immediately causes staff to resign within twenty-four hours
options.B: It can diminish intrinsic joy when rewards are removed or feel unfair
options.C: It permanently eliminates all risks of clinical medical errors
options.D: It forces hospitals to abandon all professional nursing standards

explanation: External rewards are nice, but if they stop coming, staff might lose their inner passion. True love for nursing goes beyond extra perks!

question: A new mother on the ward is bleeding heavily two hours after delivery, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Eclamptic seizure
options.B: Obstructed labor
options.C: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Uterine atony

explanation: When the uterus fails to contract firmly (atony), the blood vessels stay open and bleeding happens. A firm massage and oxytocics are usually our best friends here!

question: What are the two major parts that make up the human nervous system?

options.A: Spinal cord and vertebral column
options.B: Sympathetic and parasympathetic systems
options.C: Central and peripheral nervous systems
options.D: Brain and cranial nerves

explanation: Spot on! The nervous system splits into two main teams: the central nervous system (your brain and spinal cord) and the peripheral nervous system (all the nerves branching out to the rest of your body).

question: Why is preparing a patient for common drug side effects an important counselling objective?

options.A: It guarantees that the disease will never return again
options.B: It allows the patient to sell extra doses to others safely
options.C: It prevents patients from panicking and stopping treatment early
options.D: It eliminates all biological reactions to the medication

explanation: When patients know what mild side effects to expect, they are less likely to abandon their prescription out of fear. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h1)

question: How do SGLT2 inhibitor medications help lower your blood glucose?

options.A: By increasing the sensitivity of muscle receptors to circulating insulin
options.B: By stopping the liver from producing any new glucose molecules
options.C: By blocking renal glucose reabsorption and causing excretion in urine
options.D: By stimulating the pancreas to release extra insulin after meals

explanation: You nailed it! These drugs stop your kidneys from reabsorbing filtered sugar, so the extra glucose simply passes out through your urine.

question: What is the very first thing you should do if you accidentally prick yourself with a used needle?

options.A: Wash the puncture wound immediately with soap and running water
options.B: Squeeze the wound forcefully to bleed out all contaminated fluid
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to report the incident to management
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the injury site to trap the virus

explanation: Act fast! Wash the spot right away with soap and running water to help rinse away germs before heading to report the incident.

question: Which strategy best combines behaviorist and constructivist approaches in nursing school?

options.A: Focusing solely on the emotional well-being of students during exam weeks
options.B: Relying exclusively on silent reading assignments and standardized multiple-choice quizzes
options.C: Using skills checklists for procedural accuracy alongside simulation scenarios for clinical reasoning
options.D: Allowing students to do whatever clinical tasks they prefer without any supervision

explanation: Checklists help nail down precise steps (behaviorism), while simulation scenarios let you problem-solve and build deep understanding (constructivism). Perfect combo!

question: A surgeon has to remove the very last section of a patient's small intestine. Which part is this?

options.A: Duodenum
options.B: Ileum
options.C: Jejunum
options.D: Sigmoid colon

explanation: The ileum is the final stretch of the small intestine right before it hands over food waste to the large intestine. Great job remembering that!

question: When cleaning a hospital room, what general direction should you follow?

options.A: From the cleanest areas to the dirtiest areas
options.B: From the floor upwards to the furniture tops
options.C: From the corners towards the middle of the ceiling
options.D: Randomly based on where the most visible dust is

explanation: Well done! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you don't drag heavy dirt and germs onto surfaces you just wiped clean.

question: Which part of the ear does a tympanic thermometer aim for?

options.A: The sublingual pocket
options.B: The temporal artery
options.C: The tympanic membrane
options.D: The carotid sheath

explanation: Tympanic thermometers go gently into the ear canal to pick up heat coming straight off the eardrum.

question: If a young patient has early cervical changes but wants to have children in the future, which procedure removes the abnormal tissue while protecting her fertility?

options.A: Cervical conization
options.B: Pelvic exenteration
options.C: Total abdominal hysterectomy
options.D: Oophorectomy

explanation: You nailed it! Conization takes out a cone-shaped wedge of the cervix containing the abnormal cells. Because the rest of the uterus is left alone, future pregnancies are still possible.

question: Which protein in the blood has the shortest half-life, making it the best choice for checking recent, short-term changes in a patient's nutrition?

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Prealbumin
options.D: Transferrin

explanation: Prealbumin breaks down and builds back up really fast. This makes it a fantastic tool to show if your patient's recent meals are working within just a couple of days!

question: How is primary nursing different from traditional task-oriented nursing?

options.A: Task-oriented nursing focuses on splitting chores among staff, whereas primary nursing focuses on holistic, continuous care by one nurse.
options.B: Task-oriented nursing eliminates the need for registered nurses on the hospital floor entirely.
options.C: Primary nursing relies solely on unlicensed assistive personnel for all bedside duties.
options.D: Task-oriented nursing requires patients to change their assigned nurse every single hour.

explanation: Think of task nursing like a factory assembly line where everyone does one chore (like just giving injections), while primary nursing gives one nurse the full picture of the patient's wellbeing.

question: A patient who has been in the hospital for weeks insists they just went to the market this morning. What should you suspect?

options.A: Confabulation due to underlying memory gaps
options.B: A normal reaction to boredom in the hospital
options.C: Deliberate lying to escape hospital restrictions
options.D: Early signs of a severe bacterial meningitis

explanation: They aren't trying to pull your leg! They are confabulating—innocently making up details to fill in the blank spots in their memory.

question: What severe medical condition is directly caused by prolonged, blocked labor in young girls whose pelvises are not yet fully grown?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Obstetric fistula
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Pregnancy-induced hypertension

explanation: Well done! The baby's head presses too long against an immature pelvis, creating a hole between the birth canal and bladder or rectum. This leads to constant leakage.

question: Why are regular check-ins necessary during the MBO process?

options.A: To give supervisors an excuse to leave the wards
options.B: To find reasons to cut nurses' monthly salaries
options.C: To replace traditional paper records with computers
options.D: To see if staff need help and keep them on track

explanation: Ongoing feedback and check-ins help staff adjust their actions before it is too late to meet the goal. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h2)

question: What best describes a near-miss in a clinical environment?

options.A: An error that results in permanent patient disability
options.B: A mistake that was caught before it harmed the patient
options.C: A patient complaint about rude nursing behavior
options.D: An emergency room visit for a broken bone

explanation: A near-miss is a close call where an unsafe situation occurred, but intervention prevented it from reaching the patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T9#GNS312_U5_T9_h3)

question: What makes BMI such a popular first step in routine nursing assessments?

options.A: It provides a definitive diagnosis for metabolic syndrome
options.B: It accounts for variations in muscle mass and bone density
options.C: It is the only medically accepted way to evaluate body composition
options.D: It is quick, easy, and requires only height and weight measurements

explanation: You got this! Because you only need a patient's height and weight, BMI is super practical for busy shifts in the clinic or ward.

question: Why is it best for nurses to avoid giving false reassurance like 'everything will be fine'?

options.A: It damages trust when the patient experiences inevitable complications or pain
options.B: It forces the doctor to change the patient's medication prescription
options.C: It is against hospital policy to use comforting words with adults
options.D: It automatically increases the patient's blood pressure and heart rate

explanation: Patients know when things are tough. Being honest and supportive builds a much stronger bond than empty promises.

question: Which emergency bedside maneuver helps control bleeding temporarily by sandwiching the uterus between two hands?

options.A: External cephalic version
options.B: Controlled cord traction
options.C: Fundal displacement
options.D: Bimanual compression

explanation: Bimanual compression is a lifesaving skill! You place one hand inside the vagina and the other on the abdominal wall to squeeze the bleeding uterine walls together.

question: Why do healthcare workers sometimes feel resistant when a brand new clinical protocol is introduced?

options.A: The psychology of human beings prevents them from learning
options.B: New protocols always require less physical effort than old ones
options.C: Hospital staff universally dislike improving patient outcomes
options.D: Change disrupts established comfort zones and creates natural anxiety

explanation: It is totally normal to feel anxious when routines change. Good leaders understand this and support their teams through the transition.

question: How do clinical software apps differ from system software?

options.A: Clinical apps perform specific job tasks like charting, while system software manages the computer itself.
options.B: System software is designed for patients, while clinical apps are for doctors only.
options.C: Clinical apps can only run without an operating system present.
options.D: Clinical apps are physical hardware parts, while system software is purely digital.

explanation: Clinical apps help you do your actual job (like charting vitals), while system software keeps the machine running behind the scenes.

question: How should you respond if a client worries that injectable contraceptives cause permanent infertility?

options.A: Provide accurate education that fertility usually returns after a delay
options.B: Tell the client to ignore her worries and take the medication anyway
options.C: Refuse to give her any more supplies until she stops asking questions
options.D: Agree that fertility is permanently destroyed after one injection

explanation: Always replace myths with gentle facts! It reassures the client and respects her right to make informed choices. You're going to be a wonderful nurse.

question: Why is strict bed rest ordered during the early, active phase of myocarditis?

options.A: To lower the workload on the inflamed heart muscle
options.B: To stop blood clots from forming in the legs
options.C: To stop the kidneys from making too much urine
options.D: To keep the patient's blood pressure high

explanation: Resting lowers the heart rate and reduces the amount of work the heart has to do, giving the sore muscle time to heal. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is it so important to use simple, everyday language when teaching mothers at the clinic?

options.A: It prevents mothers from asking questions about immunization schedules
options.B: It ensures clear understanding and correct execution of home care practices
options.C: It saves clinic time so the nurse can finish work much earlier
options.D: It guarantees that mothers will memorize the entire clinic manual

explanation: You nailed it! Clear, jargon-free talk ensures mothers truly understand and can care for their babies safely at home.

question: Which variable always goes on the bottom (horizontal X-axis) of a scatter diagram?

options.A: The average median score
options.B: The dependent outcome
options.C: The independent variable
options.D: The total patient count

explanation: Remember: the independent (or explanatory) variable always sits comfortably on the horizontal X-axis.

question: Why is it important to involve men and boys in community GBV prevention programs?

options.A: To replace international aid workers in distributing food supplies
options.B: To ensure they report all female community members to the police
options.C: To take over all nursing responsibilities inside the local clinic
options.D: To help shift patriarchal attitudes and challenge harmful cultural norms

explanation: Real prevention only happens when men and boys are part of the conversation, shifting old mindsets and helping stop violence at its root.

question: Why do doctors order an MRI or CT scan for a patient suspected of having GPI?

options.A: To check the exact amount of bacteria floating in the blood
options.B: To see how well the patient's body handles penicillin
options.C: To check for brain shrinkage and rule out other causes of dementia
options.D: To prove the patient has a brand-new skin sore from syphilis

explanation: You got it! Brain scans help us spot shrinkage (atrophy) and make sure the symptoms aren't coming from a stroke, tumor, or other memory issues.

question: Which dimension of quality care ensures that services do not vary based on a client's wealth or gender?

options.A: Efficiency
options.B: Equity
options.C: Effectiveness
options.D: Timeliness

explanation: Equity ensures that the quality of care remains consistent regardless of personal characteristics like gender, wealth, or ethnicity. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h2)

question: How do standard precautions mainly stop infections from spreading?

options.A: By destroying the infectious agent inside the human body
options.B: By completely eliminating the natural reservoir of pathogens
options.C: By increasing the natural immunity of the susceptible host
options.D: By blocking the mode of transmission and portal of entry

explanation: You got it! Think of gloves and masks as road blockers. They stop germs from traveling from the patient to you, breaking the chain of infection right in the middle.

question: What type of tissue gradually replaces elastic muscle fibers in the uterus after many pregnancies?

options.A: Smooth muscle tissue
options.B: Hyaline cartilage tissue
options.C: Fibrous connective tissue
options.D: Adipose fatty tissue

explanation: With many pregnancies, the uterine muscle loses some of its stretchiness because fibrous tissue builds up, which makes the uterus contract a bit less strongly over time.

question: What is a major advantage of using topical NSAIDs instead of oral NSAIDs for older adults with osteoarthritis?

options.A: They never require a prescription from a doctor
options.B: They work within seconds to stop all joint swelling
options.C: They completely reverse the loss of joint cartilage
options.D: They have fewer systemic side effects like stomach ulcers

explanation: Topical NSAIDs deliver medicine directly to the painful joint through the skin, avoiding the high bloodstream concentrations that cause gastrointestinal bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h5)

question: What is the main job of wearable health devices in clinical care?

options.A: To deliver oral medications automatically to the patient
options.B: To diagnose complex surgical diseases without a doctor
options.C: To track and transmit health-related data continuously
options.D: To replace traditional laboratory blood testing completely

explanation: Wearables are great because they keep an eye on patient vitals between clinic visits. You've got this!

question: How do microbes mainly get around from place to place in the air?

options.A: Chemical attraction to vehicle exhaust
options.B: Magnetic pulls from the earth's core
options.C: Self-propulsion using microscopic flagella
options.D: Wind currents and air turbulence

explanation: You got it! Microbes can't fly on their own, so they completely rely on wind and moving air to carry them.

question: Which type of incontinence happens when a person leaks urine while coughing, sneezing, or lifting heavy objects?

options.A: Stress urinary incontinence
options.B: Functional urinary incontinence
options.C: Urge urinary incontinence
options.D: Overflow urinary incontinence

explanation: Stress incontinence is triggered by physical movements that suddenly push down on the bladder when pelvic support is weak. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h3)

question: Why are regular hearing tests important for workers in noisy industrial plants?

options.A: They detect early hearing loss before the damage becomes permanent
options.B: They make the factory machines run much more quietly
options.C: They prove that loud noise has no effect on human ears
options.D: They replace the need for wearing earplugs

explanation: Routine testing spots subtle hearing changes early, prompting better protection before deafness occurs. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why is a biopsy a must-have test when checking for cancer?

options.A: It replaces the need for laboratory blood testing entirely.
options.B: It lowers systemic blood pressure during diagnostic scans.
options.C: It completely cures the patient by removing all toxins.
options.D: It provides definitive microscopic proof of malignancy.

explanation: Looking at actual cells under a microscope is the only way to be 100% sure whether cancer cells are present.

question: As a nurse, what is our main goal when trying to stop a secondary injury after head trauma?

options.A: To permanently numb the patient to eliminate all pain
options.B: To reverse the torn nerve fibers caused by the initial crash
options.C: To prevent further cell death by maintaining oxygen and blood flow
options.D: To repair fractured skull bones without surgery

explanation: Well done! Since we can't always undo the initial impact, our nursing care focuses heavily on keeping oxygen and blood flowing so swelling doesn't destroy more brain cells.

question: What is the main benefit of agencies working together in community health?

options.A: It reduces the number of rural health clinics
options.B: It pools resources and expertise to tackle complex health needs
options.C: It puts all healthcare services inside major airports
options.D: It removes the need for nursing licenses

explanation: Exactly! When different agencies team up, they share funding, knowledge, and hands-on help to solve big health problems together.

question: Which of these commonly stops Nigerian women from using contraceptives?

options.A: Mandatory counseling sessions required weekly
options.B: Laws that punish women for having children
options.C: Fear of side effects and partner disapproval
options.D: An excess supply of free medications in local markets

explanation: Myths about side effects and lack of support from partners or family members are major hurdles. Gentle, accurate counseling from nurses helps clear up these fears!

question: Which of these is NOT a safe clinical improvisation in a rural clinic?

options.A: Reusing disposable single-use syringes across multiple patients to save costs
options.B: Using clean wooden boards and cloth wraps as temporary limb splints
options.C: Relying on solar-powered generators to run oxygen concentrators
options.D: Using gravity infusion sets with frequent manual checks for fluid delivery

explanation: Never reuse single-use needles or syringes! That's a major infection risk that puts patients in grave danger.

question: What is a superficial abscess?

options.A: A widespread bacterial infection of the entire muscle layer
options.B: A painless fluid-filled blister caused by a minor burn
options.C: A localized collection of pus in the skin or subcutaneous tissue
options.D: A non-inflammatory hard knot under the skin surface

explanation: An abscess is a walled-off pocket of pus that forms under the skin in response to a localized bacterial invasion. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T4#GNS311_U4_T4_h1)

question: What are the two main components that make up the cardiovascular system?

options.A: The brain and spinal cord
options.B: The heart and blood vessels
options.C: The lungs and airways
options.D: The kidneys and bladder

explanation: The cardiovascular system is composed of the heart, which acts as the pump, and blood vessels, which serve as the delivery pipes. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T1#GNS213_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must nurses care about how medications are stored on the ward?

options.A: Pharmaceutical companies only trust nurses with liquid medications
options.B: Hospital pharmacists do not understand basic ward temperature needs
options.C: Nurses handle drugs from the supply point to actual bedside administration
options.D: The law requires nurses to manufacture all ward level supplies

explanation: Spot on! You are the crucial link between the pharmacy and the patient's bedside, making drug safety a key part of your daily care.

question: Why is Guinea worm disease such a big problem for farming villages?

options.A: It causes long-term cognitive impairment in infected adults
options.B: It kills most infected working-age adults within weeks
options.C: It destroys livestock and crops stored in the village
options.D: It inflicts crippling pain that stops people from farming

explanation: Spot on! The intense pain makes it hard to walk or work, which hits farming communities hard during harvest season. You're building solid public health sense!

question: Which vaccine is routinely given during pregnancy to protect the newborn from a deadly infection?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid
options.B: Measles vaccine
options.C: Bacille Calmette-Guérin
options.D: Hepatitis A vaccine

explanation: Spot on! Tetanus toxoid is given to expectant mothers to protect their babies from neonatal tetanus. Great memory!

question: Who are the typical core members of a multidisciplinary rehabilitation team?

options.A: Only hospital administrators and billing officers
options.B: Dietitians and security personnel
options.C: Nurses, physical therapists, occupational therapists, and physicians
options.D: Pharmacists and surgical theatre technicians

explanation: Comprehensive rehabilitation relies on diverse specialists working together to address physical, medical, and functional needs. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h8)

question: What is the main tool used to see inside the tummy during a laparoscopy?

options.A: A handheld ultrasound scanner
options.B: A standard overhead operating lamp
options.C: An open surgical viewing mirror
options.D: A tiny camera called a laparoscope

explanation: You got this! A laparoscope is a thin, lighted tube with a tiny camera on the end. It sends clear pictures of the inside organs to a TV monitor for the surgeon.

question: If a pregnant mum temporarily eats less protein, what does the placenta do to protect the baby?

options.A: The placenta actively pumps amino acids to the fetus, maintaining its supply.
options.B: Amino acids turn into glucose inside the placenta.
options.C: The fetus stops growing entirely until the mother eats more meat.
options.D: Fetal amino acid levels drop immediately to match the mother's level.

explanation: Clever placenta! Even if mum's intake dips, active transport lets the placenta push extra amino acids over to keep the baby well-nourished.

question: What must a nurse have before filing a report for suspected child abuse?

options.A: Absolute physical proof and a signed confession from the parent
options.B: Written permission from the hospital legal department
options.C: Reasonable cause to suspect maltreatment based on observations
options.D: Confirmation from at least two senior medical doctors

explanation: You don't need 100% hard proof to report. A reasonable, professional suspicion based on what you see is enough to take action.

question: Why is assessing transport availability crucial before approving a home delivery?

options.A: To ensure a quick transfer if an obstetric emergency arises
options.B: So the nurse can catch a ride back to the clinic
options.C: To transport traditional birth attendants to the venue
options.D: To bring extra furniture into the room

explanation: Delays in reaching a hospital during an unexpected emergency can cost the lives of both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h6)

question: In the famous 'Swiss Cheese Model' of patient safety, what do the holes in the cheese represent?

options.A: The specific mistakes made by an individual nurse
options.B: Broken equipment waiting for replacement parts
options.C: Weaknesses and flaws in hospital safety defenses
options.D: Gaps in the patient's personal medical history

explanation: Spot on! Each slice of cheese is a safety layer, and the holes are the gaps or weaknesses. An error happens when all the holes line up at once.

question: Why must you scrub an IV port with an alcohol swab before hooking up a syringe?

options.A: It prevents the plastic port from cracking under high pump pressure
options.B: It chemically activates the medication inside the attached syringe
options.C: It removes bacteria and prevents microorganisms from entering the bloodstream
options.D: It lubricates the rubber seal so the syringe connects more smoothly

explanation: Brilliant! Friction from scrubbing wipes away germs so they don't hitch a ride straight into the patient's bloodstream.

question: A patient with hypertension stops taking their drugs because their blood pressure went back to normal. What is this called?

options.A: Erratic adherence
options.B: Creative adjustment
options.C: Premature discontinuation
options.D: Primary non-fulfillment

explanation: Stopping treatment early just because symptoms improve is called premature discontinuation. Remind your patients that the drugs are working *because* they take them!

question: Which clinical sign helps you tell kwashiorkor apart from marasmus?

options.A: Bilateral pitting edema
options.B: Extreme loss of all body fat
options.C: High serum iron concentration
options.D: Rapid increase in bone length

explanation: Remember: Kwashiorkor is tied to severe protein lack, which leads to fluid retention (pitting edema), especially making the legs and face look swollen.

question: What do we call a pregnancy where a mother is carrying two or more babies at the same time?

options.A: Singleton pregnancy
options.B: Ectopic pregnancy
options.C: Multiple pregnancy
options.D: Molar pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! A multiple pregnancy just means carrying more than one fetus—like twins, triplets, or more. You've got this!

question: How do hard structures like bones usually look on a standard ultrasound image?

options.A: As glowing green areas showing high activity
options.B: They block the sound and leave a dark shadow behind them
options.C: As completely clear, empty spaces
options.D: As bright white lines that let sound pass right through

explanation: Bone bounces most of the sound back, preventing the waves from going deeper—this creates what we call an acoustic shadow behind it.

question: What happens to a reflex if the sensory neuron gets damaged or cut?

options.A: Only the integration center will process the signal.
options.B: The brain will take over the reflex function.
options.C: The reflex response will fail to occur.
options.D: The effector will react continuously without stopping.

explanation: Think of a reflex arc like a relay race. If one runner (the sensory neuron) drops out, the message never reaches the finish line and the reflex doesn't happen.

question: Which of these is a quiet sign that a nurse might be showing bias against a PAC patient?

options.A: Providing written educational pamphlets on nutrition
options.B: Unnecessarily delaying care or withholding proper pain relief
options.C: Checking vital signs every fifteen minutes as ordered
options.D: Offering a clean hospital gown and warm blanket

explanation: Sometimes bias shows up as poor treatment—like making a patient wait too long or skipping proper pain meds because of personal judgment.

question: What is the target INR range for a standard patient taking warfarin for deep vein thrombosis?
explanation: An INR of 2.0 to 3.0 is the sweet spot for warfarin therapy—it keeps clots away without letting bleeding get out of hand. You're mastering this!

question: Why do open-air transport methods pose a threat to public health?

options.A: They expose food to dust, exhaust fumes, and animal waste
options.B: They cause food items to freeze and lose their nutritional value
options.C: They prevent regulatory agents from collecting import duties
options.D: They force farmers to harvest crops before they are ripe

explanation: Uncovered or poorly protected transit exposes edible goods to environmental pollutants and biological contaminants. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h6)

question: Why is evaluation considered an essential final step in the directing process?

options.A: It helps managers spot problems and adjust their approach for better care
options.B: It is required by law to punish nurses who make mistakes on duty
options.C: It proves to the hospital board that the manager is working hard
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any future shift planning

explanation: Continuous evaluation provides the feedback loop needed to refine leadership strategies and protect patient safety. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h8)

question: Why do patients who had a myxoma removed still need occasional follow-up scans?

options.A: To check if the lungs are growing new blood vessels
options.B: To measure how fast the patient's hair is growing
options.C: To confirm that the heart has doubled in size
options.D: To monitor for potential recurrence of the tumour over time

explanation: Even though they are benign, certain primary heart tumours can sometimes try to grow back. Routine follow-ups keep patients safe and healthy!

question: What do we call the chemical messengers that cross the synaptic cleft?

options.A: Antibodies
options.B: Neurotransmitters
options.C: Electrolytes
options.D: Plasma proteins

explanation: Neurotransmitters are the chemical bridge-builders that help a message jump across the tiny gap (synapse) from one neuron to the next.

question: Which of these features is typically seen in a female pelvis rather than a male pelvis?

options.A: A wide pubic arch
options.B: A deep, narrow cavity
options.C: Inward-projecting ischial spines
options.D: A heart-shaped pelvic inlet

explanation: Women have a nice wide pubic arch to help make room for a baby to pass through easily.

question: A post-op patient presses a handheld button on their IV machine to release a safe dose of pain meds. What is this device called?

options.A: Enteral feeding pump
options.B: Large Volume Pump

options.D: Patient-Controlled Analgesia pump

question: A patient comes to the clinic struggling with a weak urine stream after a past pelvic injury. What procedure are they most likely getting ready for?

options.A: Gastric tube insertion
options.B: Urethral dilation
options.C: Endotracheal intubation
options.D: Esophageal manometry

question: What is a major risk if a nurse crosses professional boundaries with a home care patient?

options.A: Improving the patient's physical healing speed instantly
options.B: Eliminating all paperwork requirements for the visit
options.C: Guaranteeing a promotion from the nursing agency
options.D: Compromising clinical objectivity and causing burnout

question: Why do pregnant women often complain of mild heartburn and constipation?

options.A: The kidneys stop producing gastric acid
options.B: Hormones slow down gastrointestinal motility
options.C: Dietary fiber is completely absorbed
options.D: Stomach capacity triples in size

question: Why do clinics keep a 'buffer stock' of essential drugs?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory export quotas for foreign hospitals
options.B: To hide expired medications away from visiting inspectors
options.C: To prevent running out of drugs during unexpected supply delays
options.D: To increase the financial cost of routine patient treatments

explanation: Exactly! Think of buffer stock as your safety net so the clinic never runs dry when shipments are delayed.

question: Which of these is NOT a common community myth about modern contraceptives?

options.A: They improve eyesight and physical endurance
options.B: They are foreign agents meant to reduce population
options.C: They cause permanent sterility in young women
options.D: They lead to severe congenital birth defects

explanation: Myths usually scare people by claiming contraceptives cause harm like infertility or birth defects—nobody spreads myths about them improving your eyesight!

question: Why do nurses need to check a patient's other medications when starting an antiparasitic drug that goes through the liver?

options.A: Liver enzymes completely neutralize the therapeutic effect of all parasites

options.C: Many antiparasitic drugs are metabolized by liver enzymes, altering blood levels
options.D: Hepatic enzymes prevent gastrointestinal side effects entirely

question: You check a new mother's uterus and find it feels soft and boggy instead of firm. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage her to walk in the hallway
options.B: Apply an ice pack to the perineum
options.C: Gentle fundal massage to help it contract
options.D: Give her a routine oral laxative

question: What is one big problem with planting the exact same crop over and over again on a massive scale (monoculture)?

options.A: It automatically stops all rainfall in the region
options.B: It can deplete specific soil nutrients and attract pests
options.C: It completely prevents any food from growing

explanation: Growing just one type of plant drains certain minerals right out of the dirt and sends out an open invitation to pests that love that specific plant.

question: Which nursing action prevents skin damage (shear forces) when moving a patient up in bed?

options.A: Using a draw sheet to lift the patient slightly off the mattress

question: How does carrying excess body weight contribute directly to knee osteoarthritis?

options.C: It causes the leg muscles to weaken and shrink away completely

question: Which part of the body is directly injured during the practice of FGM?

question: Which checklist type is best for checking if specific steps are done in the right order?

options.A: Task or process checklist

question: What major nutrition challenges do dietitians frequently tackle in Nigeria?

options.A: Rare genetic disorders affecting bone density in infants

options.C: Severe vitamin toxicity from over-supplementation
options.D: High rates of scurvy among coastal fishing communities

question: What medication is immediately required if a patient experiences a severe anaphylactic reaction to contrast dye?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Metformin
options.C: Aspirin
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Epinephrine is the life-saving first-line drug used to treat severe allergic reactions, opening airways and supporting blood pressure. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT legally or ethically acceptable when monitoring a public health crisis?

options.A: Ensuring fair distribution of available medical supplies to all patients
options.B: Tracking the total number of cholera cases admitted to the ward
options.C: Reporting anonymous symptom data to the local ministry of health
options.D: Broadcasting identifiable personal details of patients on public social media

question: What is the main goal of palliative care?

options.A: To speed up the dying process
options.B: To cure the underlying disease
options.C: To provide long-term rehabilitation therapy
options.D: To improve quality of life for patients and families

explanation: You've got this! Palliative care is all about bringing comfort, easing pain, and making life as good as possible for patients and their loved ones, rather than trying to cure the illness.

question: What nursing term describes when a harsh chemotherapy drug accidentally leaks out of the vein into the surrounding tissue?

options.A: Anaphylaxis

options.D: Infiltration

question: Which two major legal codes deal with criminal law across Nigeria?

question: Why are drugs like carboprost or ergometrine only given AFTER the baby is born?

options.C: They immediately stop all pain perception, making the mother unable to push

question: Which of these is a direct cost when buying medicines?

options.A: Monthly electricity bills for the pharmacy store
options.B: The invoice price paid to the drug manufacturer

options.D: Salaries paid to the hospital security guards

question: What unit of measurement do electronic IV infusion pumps typically use to set fluid rates?

options.A: Liters per 24 hours

options.D: Grams per minute

question: Which of these best describes a nominal scale of measurement?

question: Which part of the COVID-19 virus helps it attach to human cells?

question: What is the main goal of a nursing journal club in a hospital?

options.A: To raise money for the hospital's annual end-of-year party

explanation: Journal clubs are fun and supportive! They help nurses build confidence in reading and discussing research papers together. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h6)

question: You see an infected villager walking toward the local drinking pond to soothe a burning leg blister. What should you do first?

question: Why would a doctor perform a therapeutic abortion?

options.A: Fulfilling an elective personal request without medical reason
options.B: Preventing multiple births during fertility treatments
options.C: Ending a pregnancy due to financial convenience alone
options.D: Protecting maternal health or addressing severe fetal anomalies

question: Why do public health campaigns often focus mass deworming programs on school-aged children?

options.A: Children have the highest worm burdens and engage in behaviors that spread eggs

question: What should you do immediately if you find an expired drug in the crash cart during a check?

options.A: Report and replace it right away

question: What is the literal meaning of the medical term neoplasm?

options.A: Inflamed tissue

question: Why is it important for nurses to know that lymph drainage differs between the upper and lower reproductive organs?

question: Why does the body have nerve plexuses (networks of mixed nerves)?

options.A: To separate pain signals before they reach the brain

options.C: To mix nerve fibers so one minor injury doesn't totally paralyze a whole limb

question: What is the main job of Brunner's glands found in the duodenal lining?

options.A: Producing strong digestive enzymes to break down proteins

question: Which clinical finding is an early indicator of hypovolemic shock?

options.A: Rapid and weak pulse
options.B: Warm and flushed skin color
options.C: Slow and bounding pulse
options.D: High and stable blood pressure

question: What is a major duty of a Community Health Officer (CHO) at a primary health center?

options.A: Supervising junior health workers and managing clinic operations

question: Which of these is NOT checked during a care home regulatory inspection?

question: What is the main reason pregnant women experience heartburn?

question: What is the primary trigger for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)?

question: What is the main advantage of creating a weekly meal plan?

question: A nurse manager wants to involve an experienced team of senior nurses in designing a new shift roster. Which style is best?

question: Why is communication evaluated right alongside clinical nursing skills?

question: How does the body naturally balance out the forward pull of a growing belly?

question: What makes a 'cytokine storm' so dangerous in severe COVID-19 patients?

question: What is the main purpose of a questionnaire in nursing research?

question: What is the main focus of primary prevention programs for substance abuse in communities?

question: Why must nurse researchers pay close attention to ethics during explanatory studies?

question: Why are LARC methods considered very effective for post-abortion contraception?

question: What does 'unconditional acceptance' mean when practicing non-judgmental nursing?

question: What is one of the most effective nursing actions to stop the spread of resistant bugs in a ward?

question: When studying community health, what does 'incidence' mainly measure?

question: Why do we need a team of different healthcare workers at the primary health care level?

question: What usually happens to vulval varicose veins after the baby is born?

question: Which of these is considered an indirect economic barrier to getting a child immunized?

question: What is the simple difference between inter-rater and intra-rater reliability?
