options.D: There is no real difference, as both terms mean the exact same thing in research

explanation: Remember the prefixes: 'Inter-' means between different people (two nurses comparing notes), while 'intra-' means within the same person grading things over time.

question: Postmenopausal women are at a higher risk for which bone condition because their hormone levels drop?

options.A: Osteoporosis
options.B: Septic arthritis
options.C: Muscular dystrophy
options.D: Acute osteomyelitis

explanation: You got it! The drop in estrogen after menopause speeds up bone loss, putting older women at high risk for osteoporosis.

question: Which nursing goal for a malnourished patient is written clearly and measurably?

options.A: Patient will stop refusing meals when nurses enter
options.B: Patient will feel much better about hospital food soon
options.C: Patient will gain ten pounds of pure muscle by tomorrow morning
options.D: Patient will eat at least 75 percent of meals within 48 hours

explanation: Great nursing goals have a specific target (75%) and a clear timeframe (48 hours) so you can easily check your progress.

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring tracks ongoing activities, while evaluation measures final impact
options.B: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is always free
options.C: Monitoring happens after the project, while evaluation happens before
options.D: Monitoring is done by villagers, while evaluation is done by politicians

explanation: Monitoring happens continuously during the project to guide steps, while evaluation assesses overall results at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h8)

question: What would happen to the accessory sex glands if a man's testosterone levels dropped very low?

options.A: They would shrink and decrease their secretions
options.B: They would grow larger and produce excess fluid
options.C: They would immediately start producing female hormones
options.D: They would convert into urinary storage tissues

explanation: Without adequate testosterone support, these accessory organs atrophy and their secretory output drops. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which body language habit helps your patient feel trusted and relaxed during an interview?

options.A: Checking your watch frequently
options.B: Crossing your arms tightly
options.C: Maintaining an open body posture
options.D: Looking away while they speak

explanation: Well done! Keeping an open posture shows your patient you are warm, friendly, and genuinely ready to listen to their story.

question: Why must a community diagnosis look at factors like housing and clean water?

options.A: These environmental factors directly shape the health outcomes of the population
options.B: Building codes are the legal responsibility of public health nurses
options.C: Hospital administrators require these statistics for annual budgeting
options.D: Doctors use these details to prescribe specific pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Health is influenced by social, economic, and environmental conditions, not just medical care alone. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why are run charts particularly useful for busy clinical nursing units?

options.A: They require very little statistical training to read
options.B: They replace the need for writing patient care notes
options.C: They automatically dispense patient medications safely
options.D: They permanently eliminate all hospital infections

explanation: Because they are simple and visual, clinical staff can easily interpret them without needing advanced statistical skills. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h1)

question: In a UN packaging code, what does the letter 'G' tell you about the container?

options.A: It is a glass vial container
options.B: It is a fiberboard box
options.C: It is a plastic specimen bag
options.D: It is a steel liquid drum

explanation: The number 4 tells us it's a box, and G stands for fiberboard (cardboard). Simple code breaking!

question: What is the main goal of giving Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) to someone with HIV?

options.A: To replace damaged CD4 cells with donor bone marrow
options.B: To suppress viral replication to undetectable levels
options.C: To cure opportunistic infections without antibiotics
options.D: To completely eradicate the virus from every body cell

explanation: ART stops the virus from multiplying, keeping viral counts super low and protecting the immune system.

question: When is the best time to schedule morning care or physical activity for someone with rheumatoid arthritis?

options.A: Early in the morning before any medication is given while stiffness is highest
options.B: Immediately following heavy meals to ensure high energy levels
options.C: Late at night when the client is completely exhausted from the day
options.D: Right after administering morning pain medications and allowing time to take effect

explanation: Giving pain meds a little time to kick in first makes a huge difference! The patient can move around with much less pain and stiffness.

question: What does the term 'medicalization' mean when talking about female genital mutilation?

options.A: Treating FGM infections in a hospital setting
options.B: Having a trained healthcare worker perform the cutting procedure
options.C: Doing scientific research on how common the practice is
options.D: Using modern pain relief during traditional cutting

explanation: You're on point! Medicalization refers to the harmful practice of health workers performing FGM under the false belief that clinical tools make it safe.

question: As a nurse entering a brand new community, what should always be your very first step?

options.A: Listening to the community before telling them what to do
options.B: Demanding that the village head build a new health post
options.C: Distributing medications without proper medical evaluations
options.D: Issuing strict rules on sanitation and personal hygiene

explanation: Brilliant! Listening first shows respect. It helps you understand their everyday realities and priorities before you try to introduce any changes.

question: What is the most common problem that happens with multiple pregnancies?

options.A: Macrosomia
options.B: Preterm birth
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Post-term delivery

explanation: You got it! Because the womb gets stretched out so quickly, most twins decide to arrive before hitting the full 37 weeks.

question: What is the most important discharge instruction for a patient recovering from an abdominal hysterectomy?

options.A: Stop taking all prescribed pain medications immediately
options.B: Resume high-impact aerobic exercise by tomorrow
options.C: Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity for several weeks
options.D: Apply heat packs to the abdomen continuously every day

explanation: You nailed it! Resting and avoiding heavy loads protects the stitches and helps the belly heal properly inside.

question: Why do nurses join in on nutrition education programs along with food distribution efforts?

options.A: To help local governments collect taxes on agricultural goods
options.B: To teach families how to make the most of affordable, local ingredients
options.C: To replace the need for physical food supply improvements
options.D: To ensure that families stop cooking traditional meals altogether

explanation: Education helps families build healthy, balanced meals using whatever cheap, local ingredients are available around them. You're crushing these!

question: Which tool is commonly used by healthcare workers to screen older adults for signs of depression?

options.A: Body Mass Index calculator
options.B: Braden Pressure Sore Risk Scale
options.C: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.D: Geriatric Depression Scale

explanation: The Geriatric Depression Scale is a trusty questionnaire built specifically to catch early signs of depression in older populations.

question: An infection control nurse sees more wound infections popping up on a surgical ward. What should be the first step?

options.A: Close the entire hospital building permanently without telling anyone
options.B: Stop washing hands between patients to build natural immunity
options.C: Prescribe the strongest available antibiotic to every single visitor
options.D: Collect and culture samples from suspected sources to identify the causative organism

explanation: Correct! Culturing samples helps track down the root cause of an outbreak so the healthcare team can stop it in its tracks.

question: A patient develops scar tissue inside her uterus after a complicated D&C (dilation and curettage) procedure. What is this condition called?

options.A: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.B: Asherman's syndrome
options.C: Adenomyosis
options.D: Uterine didelphys

explanation: You nailed it! Asherman's syndrome refers to intrauterine adhesions or scars that typically form following surgeries inside the uterine cavity.

question: Which of the following is a core part of primary health care delivery in an IDP camp?

options.A: Managing large-scale commercial agricultural farms
options.B: Performing complex open-heart surgical procedures daily
options.C: Providing essential routine immunizations and basic medicines
options.D: Issuing international travel passports to camp residents

explanation: Primary health care is all about everyday essentials like vaccines, basic treatments, and keeping the community healthy.

question: What are the three parts of the traditional epidemiological triad?

options.A: Bacteria, virus, and fungi
options.B: Patient, nurse, and doctor
options.C: Symptoms, diagnosis, and treatment
options.D: Agent, host, and environment

explanation: You will see this triad everywhere in public health! It looks at how the disease agent interacts with the vulnerable host (the person) and their surrounding environment.

question: Why must nurse managers verify a new applicant's license with the regulatory council?

options.A: To check if the nurse prefers morning or night shifts
options.B: To see which secondary school the nurse attended
options.C: To confirm the nurse is legally authorized to practice
options.D: To find out how much salary the nurse was paid previously

explanation: License verification protects patients by ensuring only legally certified and qualified professionals provide care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h3)

question: A ward successfully tested a new handoff communication checklist with one nurse for a week. What is the most logical next step?

options.A: Immediately fire all staff who refuse to use the old checklist
options.B: Expand the test to include all nurses on that specific shift for another week
options.C: Abandon the checklist because testing is now complete
options.D: Mandate the checklist for every hospital in the entire country immediately

explanation: You nailed it! Scaling up should happen step-by-step—moving from one person to a small group before trying a wider rollout.

question: What tool do managers commonly use to track progress toward objectives?

options.A: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
options.B: Random patient complaint letters
options.C: Daily weather forecasts
options.D: Personal diary entries

explanation: KPIs provide measurable data that helps managers track whether goals are being met. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the common first-line vitamin supplement used alongside an antihistamine to treat pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Vitamin D3
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Vitamin B6
options.D: Vitamin B12

explanation: Pyridoxine, or Vitamin B6, is widely recommended as a safe and effective starting medication for pregnancy nausea. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h5)

question: What is the main job of the large intestine in our daily digestion?

options.A: Producing bile to break down fats
options.B: Absorbing water and compacting waste
options.C: Secreting digestive enzymes for proteins
options.D: Mixing food with stomach acid

explanation: As food waste travels through, the large intestine pulls out the remaining water, turning liquid into solid stool. Spot on!

question: Which age group is most commonly affected by febrile seizures?

options.A: Adolescence to early adulthood
options.B: Advanced old age
options.C: Birth to three months
options.D: Six months to five years

explanation: Febrile seizures typically occur in young children whose developing nervous systems react strongly to rapid temperature increases. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is an appropriate immediate nursing intervention for a newborn diagnosed with a skull injury?

options.A: Place the infant flat without any head support
options.B: Minimize handling to prevent further trauma
options.C: Encourage vigorous crying to expand the lungs
options.D: Perform daily head massage to reduce swelling

explanation: Reducing unnecessary handling and stimulation helps protect the injured skull and prevents spikes in intracranial pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h5)

question: How does the Contributory Pension Scheme work for nursing personnel in the public sector?

options.A: Employees manage their pension funds independently without any institutional oversight
options.B: Both the employer and employee contribute funds monthly to a Pension Fund Administrator
options.C: Retirement benefits are paid as a lump sum immediately upon completing probation
options.D: The government pays the entire retirement fund without any employee deduction

explanation: Both you and the government put money into your pension account every month so you are financially secure when you retire.

question: What makes a disease communicable?

options.A: It only affects people living in tropical climates.
options.B: It can be spread from one person or host to another.
options.C: It is caused strictly by genetic mutations in the body.
options.D: It cannot be prevented by standard hygiene practices.

explanation: You've got this! Communicable diseases simply mean infections that can jump or spread from an infected person to someone else. Keep up the great work!

question: A home health nurse notices an older patient's pension checks are missing and lights are cut off despite having funds. What is going on here?

options.A: Physical neglect
options.B: Active abandonment
options.C: Financial exploitation
options.D: Emotional maltreatment

explanation: Taking or misusing a vulnerable person's money or resources is financial exploitation. You're building great clinical intuition!

question: What physical sign is tested by tapping the facial nerve near the cheek to check for low calcium?

options.A: Trousseau's sign
options.B: Brudzinski's sign
options.C: Chvostek's sign
options.D: Homans' sign

explanation: A quick tap on the facial nerve causing the cheek or lip to twitch is a classic positive Chvostek's sign, pointing to low calcium!

question: What is the main benefit of community-based rehabilitation (CBR)?

options.A: It completely stops patients from ever visiting a hospital
options.B: It removes the need for support from family members
options.C: It brings healthcare services right into the patient's local environment
options.D: It focuses only on surgical procedures

explanation: You got it! CBR makes care super accessible because it meets patients where they live, making it easier for them to join in and transition back to everyday life.

question: Why should a patient wear lightweight cotton clothing inside a steam tent instead of heavy synthetics?

options.A: Heavy clothes block the steam from reaching the lungs
options.B: Cotton fabrics absorb all the humidity completely
options.C: Cotton breathes better and prevents overheating
options.D: Synthetic fabrics melt easily when exposed to steam

explanation: Exactly! Cotton keeps the patient comfortable and stops them from getting too hot in a humid space.

question: Why do incubatory carriers give nurses headaches when trying to stop the spread of disease?

options.A: They spread pathogens before anyone realizes they are sick
options.B: They only transmit infections through contaminated drinking water
options.C: They carry drug-resistant bacteria that resist all antibiotics
options.D: They refuse to take their prescribed medications in the ward

explanation: Since they look and feel healthy right now, nobody suspects they are passing germs around until symptoms finally show up later.

question: What do we call the method where the nurse shows a procedure and the patient does it back?

options.A: Demonstration and return demonstration
options.B: Trial and error
options.C: Group brainstorming
options.D: Lecture and silent reflection

explanation: Correct! Showing them first and then watching them do it lets you spot and fix mistakes right away.

question: Which of these is most likely to make people refuse to join a community insurance scheme?

options.A: A lack of trust in the managers handling the funds
options.B: Excessive availability of free medication
options.C: Too many doctors working in local health clinics
options.D: High levels of income among farmers

explanation: Trust is everything! If community members don't trust the people managing the money, they simply won't invest their hard-earned cash into the health scheme.

question: What is a key nursing care action for a patient dealing with extreme fatigue from disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Keeping the patient confined strictly to bed
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake after midday
options.C: Scheduling planned rest periods throughout the day
options.D: Encouraging intense daily marathon training

explanation: Pacing is everything! Balancing daily activities with scheduled rest helps patients conserve their energy without burning out.

question: A nurse wants to check a patient's light touch feeling on their legs. What is the best tool to use?

options.A: A cold metal stethoscope bell pressed firmly
options.B: A wisp of cotton stroked lightly over the skin
options.C: A sterile needle poked deep into the muscle
options.D: A low-frequency tuning fork on the patella

explanation: Correct! Gently brushing a cotton wisp across the skin is a classic, gentle way to test light touch pathways without causing discomfort.

question: Why do we study occupational health risks in nursing?

options.A: To help nurses stay safe and maintain a healthy career
options.B: To reduce the financial expenses of the hospital management
options.C: To eliminate all physical tasks from daily nursing duties
options.D: To ensure patients recover faster from their illnesses

explanation: Spotting workplace hazards early helps you protect your own health so you can enjoy a long, injury-free nursing journey. You matter too!

question: What is the main job of extra protein during pregnancy?

options.A: Regulating sudden shifts in blood pressure
options.B: Preventing common digestive discomforts
options.C: Building uterine, breast, and fetal tissues
options.D: Providing quick energy for the mother's brain

explanation: Nailed it! Protein acts like the primary building blocks for the baby's growth, plus the mum's changing uterus and breasts.
